profile_text.body:
The Algorithmic Justice League is a nonprofit founded in 2016 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Its site states that its mission is to raise awareness about the impacts of AI, equip advocates with empirical research, build the voice and choice of the most impacted communities, and galvanize researchers, policy makers, and industry practitioners to mitigate AI harms and biases. The organization describes itself as building a movement to shift the AI ecosystem toward equitable and accountable AI.

The site argues that AI can amplify racism, sexism, ableism, and other forms of discrimination, and that AI systems are used to decide who gets hired, the quality of medical treatment people receive, and whether someone becomes a suspect in a police investigation. It says such tools can harm vulnerable and marginalized people and threaten civil rights, and calls for accountable and equitable AI. On facial recognition, it notes that the TSA is expanding use of the technology in airports and that travelers can opt out, and it asks people to share their experiences with airport face scans.

The organization says it began as the subject of the Coded Bias film, which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2020 and highlights people affected by harmful technology. Its site also asks for monthly sustainers. No products or lawsuits are recorded for the organization.
